About

The storybehind the room.

Reality Center opened in Santa Monica at the beginning of 2022, in a brick building that once held the city's municipal offices. What happens inside it started a long way from here.

Leadership

Two paths.The same mission.

Reality Center grew from two paths into the same mission: Tarun Raj's drive to make transformative wellness more accessible, and Jonathan Chia's lived experience as a veteran searching for a way to move beyond survival mode.

Tarun came to this from motion graphics and experiential design. Around 2012 he found himself running a 10,000 square foot arts and education space in South Central Los Angeles, and it was there he first sat in front of the technology: someone chanting into a microphone, the words turning into vibration you could see on a screen, hear through speakers, and — to his surprise — feel through the chair. He has described that moment as the point the work stopped being a curiosity. Technology could do more than entertain.

Jonathan came to it from fifteen months of combat in Iraq, and from what happened after. He served through Operation Iraqi Freedom and Operation Enduring Freedom, and lost friends — in theatre, and then at home. He has spent more than a decade since building alternative therapies for people carrying post-traumatic stress, and sits on the executive boards of three veteran-focused nonprofits.

The technology became a meaningful part of Jonathan's own change. Reality Center grew from a belief that more people should have access to that same possibility.

Mission

Technology that facilitatespositive change.

Reality Center exists to provide technology that facilitates positive change for humanity — and to put tools that improve mental, physical and spiritual wellness within reach of far more people than can currently get to them.

Sensory Resonance

Where the technologycomes from.

The work rests on a theory called Sensory Resonance, published in 1990 by co-founder Don Estes — a medical technologist, laboratory director and neuroscientist who spent decades developing frequency instruments before any of this had a storefront. The theory holds that for every outer sensory mechanism there is an inner one.

When all the senses are synchronised, the body reaches a state that is both relaxing and inspiring. Estes called that state Sensory Resonance. Everything here — the light, the score, the WaveTable — exists to make it easier to find.

Reality Center is the implementation, not the invention. The founding group is Tarun Raj, Benji Tucker, Don Estes and Jonathan Chia, and the technology reflects more than thirty years of development that predates all of it.

A short history

How it got here.

  • 1990
    Sensory Resonance is published. Don Estes sets out the theory that for every outer sense there is an inner one — the basis for everything that follows.
  • 1990s–2010s
    Three decades of instruments. Estes designs, builds and operates a succession of sensory facilities, developing the light, sound and vibration hardware that the WaveTable descends from.
  • 2012
    Tarun Raj meets the technology. In a warehouse arts space in South Central Los Angeles, a chanted voice becomes something visible, audible and physical at the same moment.
  • 2022
    Reality Center opens. A converted municipal building a block from the Santa Monica pier, built around a room of WaveTables facing a projection wall.
  • 2022–
    Operation Reset begins. With support from the Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health, the veteran program starts running sessions for those who served and their families.

Initiatives

Not everyonecan walk in the door.

So we go to them. Four programs, for people whose nervous systems took the weight of something the rest of us only read about — veterans, families burned out of their homes, foster teens, and teams who run hot for a living.

Operation Reset

A multi-sensory resilience
program for veterans.

With the support of the Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health, Reality Center runs a biofeedback program built for veterans and their families — for post-traumatic stress, military sexual trauma, and combat-related experience.

Sessions are peer-supported and run as a cohort, because the connection between people in the room turns out to matter as much as what happens on the table.

  • FormatA guided three-hour workshop: preparation and breathwork, the multi-sensory session, integration, then food with your cohort.
  • IncludedInTune, a voice-based meditation tool you keep using at home, and follow-up from experienced veteran and expert peers.
  • PartnersLos Angeles County Department of Mental Health · Veteran Care Group
Learn about Operation Reset
Fire Aid LA

For those affected by the
LA fires, our doors are open.

Los Angeles has been carrying a lot. For many families affected by the fires, the hardest part is what happens after. The stress. The anxiety. The sleepless nights.

At Reality Center, we believe healing starts by creating safety in the body. Complimentary light, sound and vibration sessions are open to individuals and families affected by the Palisades, Eaton, Altadena and Sandy fires.

  • WhoAnyone who lost a home, is displaced, is carrying significant hardship, or worked the fires as an emergency services worker.
  • FormatSingle, couple or group — up to four participants per group, up to three sessions.
  • CostNone.
Request support
Wolf Connection

For young people who
never got to feel safe.

Wolf Connection runs a ranch north of Los Angeles where foster and at-risk teens work alongside rescued wolfdogs — animals that were also failed by somebody. The kids learn to read an animal that will not pretend. The animal learns a person can be trusted. It works because neither side can fake it.

We take the same young people through sessions here. Different method, same target: teaching a body that has been braced for years that it is allowed to stand down. One approach uses an animal. Ours uses light, sound and vibration. Together they reach kids that neither would reach alone.

  • WhoFoster youth and at-risk teens referred through Wolf Connection’s existing programs. [CONFIRM — age range and referral route]
  • FormatSessions at the Santa Monica center, alongside their work at the ranch. [CONFIRM — cohort size and number of sessions]
  • CostNone to the young people or their carers.
Workplace Wellness

Bring this
to your team.

Custom performance programs designed to support employee well-being, improve team cohesion and lift performance — delivered at the Santa Monica center.

The core format is Team Biohacking: a two-hour immersive session your whole team goes through together, with time afterwards to talk about it.

  • Two hoursFifteen minutes of guided meditation and intention-focused breathwork, an hour of sensory therapy, then thirty minutes of sharing and questions.
  • AfterExercises to continue with, and personalised integration with Reality Center staff.
  • ReportedIn a recent survey, users of our technology reported a 70% reduction in stress in the week following their first session. [VERIFY — sample size and survey date are not published.]
